mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing the present value of future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.5% in a 3-month window, it signals an imminent monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate and falling unemployment rate indicates a tightening monetary policy amid strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate profit margins.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp in 3 months AND UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (below 4.5%), the labor market tightness leads to wage pressures that increase corporate costs and reduce profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts indicate strong consumer demand for residential construction, which typically signals robust economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth falls below 0.5% annually, it signals a weakening manufacturing sector that reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong retail sales growth (above 0.8% monthly), consumer spending momentum drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS growth exceeds 0.8%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment growth and falling unemployment rate indicates a tightening labor market that increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly AND UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition.
